hints: Focus on what makes a sigma bond different from a pi bond, every single bond is one sigma, while each double bond is one sigma plus one pi.
Start by counting the skeleton, there are 6 C-C or C-O single links plus 3 double bonds, each of which still contributes one sigma bond.
Now add all the C-H sigma bonds to your skeleton count, remember each CH2 has two and each CH has one, then total them to finish.
walkthrough:
**Recall the sigma rule**

Think simply first. Every bond starts with one sigma bond. A single bond is 1 sigma, a double bond is 1 sigma + 1 pi.

Rule to use:
$$\text{single = 1 } \sigma, \quad \text{double = 1 } \sigma + 1 \pi$$

**Count the heavy atom skeleton**

Look at the chain $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$. Ignore H for a moment.

Skeleton sigma bonds:
$$3 \times (\text{C=C or C=O}) = 3 \sigma + 3 \pi$$
$$5 \times (\text{C-C or C-O single}) = 5 \sigma$$
So skeleton gives $3 + 5 = 8$ sigma bonds.

**Count the C-H sigma bonds**

Each H makes one single bond, so one sigma. Count them carefully from the formula.

Left side: $\text{CH}_2$ has 2, $\text{CH}$ has 1, $\text{CH}_2$ has 2. Right side: $\text{CH}_2$ has 2, $\text{CH}$ has 1, $\text{CH}_2$ has 2.
$$\text{C-H } \sigma = 2+1+2+2+1+2 = 10$$

**Add to get the total**

Now put skeleton and C-H together. This is where students often forget one CH2 group.
$$\text{total } \sigma = 8 \text{ (skeleton)} + 10 \text{ (C-H)} = 18$$

options.A: 15 is too low. It usually comes from missing several C-H sigma bonds or forgetting that each double bond still contains one sigma bond. Every H shown is one sigma.
options.B: 17 is one short. This is the classic miscount trap, often from missing one C-H bond or one C-C / C-O single sigma bond when rushing the long chain.
options.C: 18 is correct. Skeleton gives 8 sigma (5 singles + 3 from the double bonds) and C-H bonds give 10 sigma, for 8 + 10 = 18 total sigma bonds.
options.D: 21 is the total number of bonds (sigma + pi). There are 18 sigma + 3 pi = 21. The question asks for sigma only, so you must not count the 3 pi components of the two C=C and one C=O bonds.
